widgetMetadata.instructions: Each entry under `widgets` describes one chart/widget rendered on this page of the Israeli Ecosystem dashboard. Descriptions are result-agnostic: they explain what the visualization shows and how to interpret it, not the specific numbers. The `dataPaths` array on each entry lists dot-notation paths inside this same JSON file where the underlying data for that widget lives (e.g. "kpis.patentingStartups" or "ipIntensity.items") When summarizing or answering questions about a number from this snapshot, locate the relevant widget(s) by `dataPaths` and quote the corresponding `description` to explain the metric. Widgets that have a 10 year trend usually show the total overall (across all years) and you get the exact data for each year in the past 10 years. The 10 year data do not add up to the total of course

startups:map.title: Israel Startup Map
startups:map.description: Geographic distribution of Israeli startups by their registered address in Israel. Each city marker is sized by the number of startups with an active legal registration in that city and colored by its administrative district. The legend lists the same totals by district. Only startups with a known registered Israeli address appear.

startups:kpi-total-startups.title: Total Startups
startups:kpi-total-startups.description: Total number of Israeli startups in the dataset (active, exited, and closed combined). The bar chart shows new startups by founding year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-funding-rounds.title: Funding Rounds
startups:kpi-funding-rounds.description: Total number of equity rounds raised by Israeli startups across all time: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the count of rounds closed each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-total-raised.title: Total Raised
startups:kpi-total-raised.description: Total capital (USD) Israeli startups raised in equity rounds: money paid into the company for newly issued shares, from pre-seed through late stage, including SAFEs, convertible notes and bridges. The bar chart shows the dollar amount raised each year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-acquisitions.title: Acquisitions
startups:kpi-acquisitions.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via a completed acquisition, meaning a deal that actually went ahead. The bar chart shows acquisitions by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-ipos.title: IPOs
startups:kpi-ipos.description: Total number of Israeli startups that exited via IPO and reached the market, meaning shares priced or trading on a public exchange. The bar chart shows IPOs by exit year over the past 10 years.

startups:kpi-time-to-exit.title: Time to Exit
startups:kpi-time-to-exit.description: Average number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, capped at 30+ years.

startups:survival-distribution.title: Survival Distribution
startups:survival-distribution.description: Breakdown of all Israeli startups by current status: Active (still operating), Closed (shut down or dissolved), and Exit (acquired or went public). The center of the donut shows the total number of startups, or the value of the hovered slice.

startups:exit-funnel.title: Exit Funnel
startups:exit-funnel.description: How many Israeli startups make it through each progressive milestone toward an exit: All startups (everyone in the dataset), Funded (raised at least one equity round), $1M+ (raised at least $1 million in total), $10M+ (raised at least $10 million in total), Exit (a completed acquisition or public listing). The percentage on each segment is the retention from the All-startups stage.

startups:time-to-exit.title: Time To Exit
startups:time-to-exit.description: Average and median number of years between founding year and exit year (acquisition or IPO) across all exited Israeli startups. The histogram below shows the distribution of those exit times in 1-year buckets, with the rightmost bucket capturing every exit at 30 or more years.

startups:industry-mix.title: Industry Share Over Time
startups:industry-mix.description: Stacked bar chart of the industry mix of Israeli startups by founding year. Each bar is one year, broken into 6 industry categories (IT and Telecom, Healthcare and Food, Consumer Goods and Services, Energy and Utilities, Financial Services, Media and Entertainment). Sub-industries that fall outside these 6 are bucketed into Unknown and excluded from the visible mix. The legend on the right shows each industry overall total and share across all years.

startups:signal-deeptech.title: Deeptech
startups:signal-deeptech.description: Share of Israeli startups flagged as deeptech. Deep tech companies require significant resources, long development cycles, specialized expertise, and substantial investment. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of deeptech startups.

startups:signal-global.title: Operating Globally
startups:signal-global.description: Share of Israeli startups that have a product with a global audience. The 10-segment meter visualizes that share. The number on the right is the absolute count of globally operating startups.

startups:trending-up.title: Sub-Industries Trending Up By Share Of Total
startups:trending-up.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has grown the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:trending-down.title: Sub-Industries Trending Down By Share Of Total
startups:trending-down.description: Top 5 sub-industries whose share of new Israeli startups has shrunk the most over the past 10 founding years. Each line is one sub-industry. The value at year Y is the share of startups founded in year Y whose primary sub-industry falls in that group. The dashed tail marks the most recent year, which is still incomplete.

startups:feed-funding.title: Funding Feed
startups:feed-funding.description: Latest funding rounds added to the dataset, gathered from multiple verifiable sources. Unlike the headline funding figures, this feed carries every round type, grants and venture debt included, each one flagged with isNonEquity so you can tell them apart.

startups:feed-new-startups.title: New Startups
startups:feed-new-startups.description: Latest startups added to the dataset. Not necessarily new Startups founded.

startups:feed-notable.title: Notable Events
startups:feed-notable.description: Latest notable events gathered form news feeds, including acquisitions, IPOs, corporate events, strategic partnerships and more.

newStartups.description: QR-code based in-room ordering platform for hotels that lets guests order room service from their phones, routes orders to staff screens tagged with room numbers, provides automatically translated menus, and includes a live dashboard for revenue and order trends.
Online magazine covering culture, entertainment, food and urban leisure, providing editorial articles, reviews and recommendations for readers in Tel Aviv and across Israel

Designs, manufactures and supplies industrial and commercial lighting systems for engineering projects, combining local production and repair with controlled imports built to engineering specifications.
Procurement and materials management platform for construction contractors that helps trade and self-perform contractors order, track and manage materials across projects from planning to payment.

Fractional investment platform enabling retail investors to buy partial ownership in alternative and luxury assets including watches, jewellery, art, classic cars and property through an online platform.

Software platform that helps destination management companies and tour operators convert itinerary content into branded proposals and a connected experience for guides and travelers, with AI-assisted drafting and sharing through a traveler app.

Consumer mobile app that helps users claim compensation for cancelled, delayed or changed flights and for unsolicited spam and marketing messages. With explicit permission it scans email and text messages to detect qualifying notices and generates an evidence report, then connects users to licensed attorneys for case review.
Online brand offering baby and child safety products for parents and caregivers purchasing through e-commerce channels.

AI-native real estate platform that lets renters search rentals in plain language, apply online, book viewings, and sign contracts digitally in one place, while giving agents and landlords tools to manage listings, leads, viewings, and contracts in one pipeline.
Designs and manufactures modular open-baffle loudspeakers for audiophiles and music enthusiasts, with configurable speaker sets, hand-finished wood options and tool-less assembly for home listening.
AI-native learning platform offering a conversational AI tutor app for mobile devices that delivers personalised lessons for adult learners preparing for exams, licences and career goals.

Technology training provider offering work-integrated programs in software engineering, AI and data science, and cybersecurity, combining immersive coursework with paid apprenticeships and part-time certificates for working professionals.

AI-powered supply chain operations platform that assesses part-level risk for complex, BOM-driven hardware manufacturers. It analyzes supplier communications, internal supply chain data and external signals to surface prioritized actions tied to builds, customers and revenue.

Enterprise data management platform using blockchain, cloud and IoT technologies to enable inter-company data collaboration and privacy governance, alongside a new-business support service for large enterprises.
Mobile application that aggregates short sports highlights videos, allowing fans to watch key moments from multiple matches in brief clips in one place instead of browsing for them across sources.
Provider of rugged trail and security camera systems with AI based image analysis, real time alerts and remote management for security, enforcement, monitoring and research applications
Online marketplace selling discounted digital game keys, software keys, in-game currencies and subscriptions for PC and console platforms, delivered digitally by email.
Online relationship coaching platform providing on-demand dating and relationship advice from trained coaches via call, text and chat for individuals and couples.

Communications company providing push to talk over cellular services, cloud based IoT temperature and humidity monitoring, digital radio systems and custom wireless product development, with end to end supply and support for organizational customers.
Automated tuition management software for preschools, kindergartens and educational institutions, covering registration, tuition calculation, billing, collections and student and staff management.

notable.summary: Starling Systems entered a reseller partnership with Dwyka Mining Services to introduce Starling's Pathfinder-X drone-in-a-box aerial intelligence and autonomous capabilities to the African mining industry, including surface surveys, perimeter security alongside Boston Dynamics Spot, and underground laser-navigation missions.

Wholly owned subsidiary Eco Wave Power U.S. Inc. signed a three-year MoU with WISeQey Corp., SEALSQ Corp. and SEALCOIN AG, demonstrating trusted digital twin and authenticated automated energy transactions using the Jaffa Port installation, targeting applications for AI data centers.

Bria laid off approximately 20 of its 60 employees as part of a corporate restructuring, halting development of its FIBO foundation model due to cost against better-funded rivals and pivoting to its Bria Create enterprise marketing platform. Model development was consolidated in Israel, VP of Research Ron Mokady departed, VP of Business Amit Goldenberg moved to an advisory role, and CTO Misha Feinstein took charge of R&D.
Acquired Fireberry, expanding its business management portfolio and accelerating its AI-first vision for the future of business management.

Introduced new AI capabilities for smart accessibility management in software development, including the Accessibility Guru feature that identifies and fixes accessibility issues at source-code level using AI agents, integrated with VS Code and AI development tools such as Claude, GitHub and Copilot, connecting accessibility testing, CI/CD systems and enterprise governance in an Accessibility Orchestration approach.

Appointed Rogerio Rizzi as Executive Vice President of Corporate Strategy and Development. Rizzi joined from Okta, Inc., where he established the Corporate Strategy team and ran growth strategy for six years, and previously led Corporate Strategy at SAP SE and Hewlett Packard Enterprise.

Launched the Sapphire infusion pump system in Japan in partnership with ParagonCare Japan, following PMDA regulatory approval, expanding access across hospital, ambulatory, and homecare settings in the Asia-Pacific market.

Eitan Medical announced a strategic partnership with Paragon Medtech to launch the Sapphire infusion platform in Japan, entering the Japanese market through Paragon Medtech's local regulatory and distribution network.

Launched AI Shopping Assistant, a WooCommerce chat plugin that searches the catalogue (including misspelt queries), answers product and policy questions from the store's own pages, builds a real WooCommerce cart and hands off to checkout, answers order-status questions for logged-in customers, and offers an optional admin read-only store assistant. Launch offer code AISA40 (40% off) runs until 30 November 2026, licences from $79.

Acquired by Priority Software. Priority announced the acquisition of a majority stake (more than 50% of shares, with an option to purchase the remaining stake from founder and CEO Amir Segev) in Fireberry, valuing the company at over NIS 100 million (over $30 million). The deal expands Priority's AI-native cloud ERP portfolio with Fireberry's AI-powered CRM platform.

Extended the platform to citizen developers with Citizen Developer Security (currently in private preview), discovering every AI builder and unmanaged codebase, protecting devices and AI sessions, and securing agent-generated applications.

Plurai introduced SCOPE (Symbolic Composition Over Predicates and Extractors), a framework that compiles natural-language policies into executable programs built from weak-model predicates, deterministic extractors and composing Python code, optimized with adversarial counterexamples. It matches frontier reasoning models at a fraction of the cost with more stable predictions, and is available as part of the Plurai SDK, with a paper on arXiv and a benchmark released on HuggingFace.
Launched Descope Envoy, a delegated access product for personal AI agents, enabling secure delegated sign-in and authorization for agents acting on a user's behalf.

Appointed Liron Shtraichman as Chief R&D Officer and Guy Havusha as Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). Both join from monday.com, where Shtraichman led global engineering through its AI-native transformation and Havusha served as Global CISO.

Signed its first reseller agreement with Sistran under an expanded global channel strategy, initially focusing on Brazil before expanding across Latin America, to make its intelligent decisioning solutions more accessible to insurers through Sistran's regional presence of more than 105 customers in 18 countries.

Torii released a major update to Eko, its agentic governance assistant, adding deeper context awareness, pattern recognition across the customer's SaaS and AI environment, contract Q&A, vendor comparisons, and approved actions. Eko is available in the Torii app, in Slack, and via MCP.

Launched Dragonfly Enterprise: starting with v2.1 the product moves from BSL 1.1 to a new source-available license, free for production use up to 100 vCPUs with commercial licensing above that, and all future development ships in Dragonfly Enterprise.

Duane Mancini, M.Sc. (CEO and Co-Founder of Project Medtech, host of the Project Medtech Podcast) appointed to the epm Therapeutics Board of Directors, announced by the company. He brings experience in regulatory strategy, clinical trial design and commercialization for medical technology, and will advise as EPM301 advances toward clinical development for Prader-Willi syndrome hyperphagia.
Tanium joined OpenAI's Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) program, applying OpenAI GPT Cyber Models to threat research, vulnerability and remediation research, and the security of the Tanium platform.

Torii Research published its November 2026 editions of three usage-data rankings: the Adoption Index, the AI Breakout (in which ElevenLabs climbed to #14), and the Shadow IT Index (led by TypeSafe AI), built from anonymized aggregated SaaS usage data.
